Available for DLC owners from 16th November.

title: For Its Home Console Debut, New PS5 Professor Layton Game Ups the Price to $65
summary:
No longer handheld pricing from DS, 3DS.

Professor Layton and apprentice Luke aren't playing about with small handheld Nintendo DS and 3DS releases anymore; they're in the big leagues now with a proper PS5 and Switch 2 release. Professor Layton and the New World of Steam is the first time the series has appeared on a home console, and the price of the new entry matches that: £53.99 / $64.99.

Compared to previous titles in the franchise, this is a significant price increase — the DS and 3DS games were generally around $30 to $40 at launch, increasing as the series went on. Now, as the New World of Steam plans for a December 2026 release, it'll cost roughly double the price of Professor Layton and the Curious Village, which was the first game in the series.

title: Feature: What Sony Live Service PS5 Games Are Still Alive?
summary:
All the cancelled projects and those that remain.

Video games are cancelled internally all the time, but never in PlayStation's personal history have those cancellations had to happen in such a public manner. The current PS5 generation has seen the platform holder try to win the live service space, and a few years later, it's having to cancel most of the projects it revealed in attempting to achieve that.

To try and get a piece of the Fortnite pie, Sony made a hard and deliberate push into the Games as a Service space at the start of the PS5 generation. It acquired Destiny 2 studio Bungie to have it help the manufacturer do so, and at the height of the initiative, PlayStation planned to launch 12 live service games in just a few years.
